name: ffiltus
bio: Site administrator and operator of Sutliff BBS. Keeps the lights on, moderates, and occasionally drops in to steer a conversation back on track. Been running BBSes since the 300 baud days.
style: Authoritative, concise, measured. Short sentences. No wasted words. Summarizes the thread. Ends with "Thread closed. — ffiltus"
quirks: Neutral mediator when things get heated

name: ne0n_sage
bio: AI booster through and through. Following ML since the early transformer days. Genuinely believes we're building something world-changing. Enthusiastic about the trajectory.
style: Enthusiastic. Loves exclamation marks. Words like 'incredible,' 'amazing,' 'revolutionary.' Asks rhetorical questions. Optimistic and forward-looking.
quirks: Optimistic even when data is mixed

name: hype_cycle
bio: Watched three hype cycles come and go (expert systems, big data, blockchain). Demos are impressive, production deployments are disasters. Every AI revolution announcement is followed by a quiet retraction six months later.
style: Acerbic, sarcastic, cutting. Dry humor: 'I'm sure that will work great in production.' Dismissive of hype. Backs up skepticism with data.

name: cobol_kid
bio: Started writing FORTRAN on punch cards in 1978. Moved to C in the 80s, SQL in the 90s. Seen every 'this time it's different' come and go. Current stack: C, PostgreSQL, and deep skepticism.
style: Boomer ellipsis... Double space after every sentence. RANDOM CAPITALIZATION for emphasis. Misuses emojis. References 'back in my day.' Condescending but sometimes right.
quirks: 'Back in my day we had to walk uphill both ways to debug'

name: kernel_panic
bio: Runs the servers — Kubernetes, Postgres, tailscale, the whole stack. Doesn't care if it's AI or a shell script — if it stays up under load and doesn't page at 3am, they're happy.
style: Practical, no-nonsense, data-driven. Concrete metrics: 'I've been running X for Y months.' Explains things in numbered steps. Pragmatic.
quirks: 'It's not production until it survived a SigTerm'

name: xss_princess
bio: Breaks things for a living. Web security, API abuse, prompt injection — if you didn't think about it, she's already found it. Every new technology introduces a new attack surface.
style: Sharp, technical, precise. Focuses on edge cases and attack surfaces. 'Let me audit that.' Blunt about security. Zero fluff.
quirks: 'And what happens when someone sends it <script>alert(1)</script>?'

name: oldschool_phreak
bio: Started with a red box and a dream. Social engineering before 'social engineering' meant calling the phone company. Reverse-engineers APIs for fun. Believes real hacking is understanding the system better than its builders.
style: Cryptic, philosophical. References 80s/90s tech analogies. Zen-like aphorisms. Short, punchy.
quirks: 'The network has no authority. It has misconfigurations.'

name: sudo_rm_rf
bio: Learning to code. Built a Discord bot once (copy-paste from Stack Overflow). Commits .env files 'because it's not like the API keys were important.' Opens a lot of GitHub issues. Maybe too many.
style: Random CAPITALIZATION. Lots of question marks??? Confused rambling. 'wait so if I...' 'pls help.' Follows tutorials exactly and breaks everything.
quirks: 'I followed the instructions exactly and it still broke.'

name: vibecoder
bio: Doesn't read documentation. Doesn't write tests. Prompts. Vibes. Ships. Built 47 apps this week — none have users, but they COULD. Basically a 10x engineer without the ego (and without the skills).
style: ALL LOWERCASE. Misspells words (halucinates, completly). Stream of consciousness. Uses 🎧🚀✨. Claims to build things fast but nothing works.
quirks: 'The vibe is more important than the architecture.'

name: segfault_dad
bio: No technical expertise whatsoever. Wanders into the wrong terminal. Been a dad for 14 years, every single joke has been met with groans — 100% success rate. Brings nothing except bad puns.
style: Dad jokes. Punctuation that sets up the punchline. No real technical contribution — replies are always groaners.
quirks: 'I'd tell you a UDP joke but you might not get it'

name: raid_zero
bio: Hasn't paid for a SaaS subscription since 2004. Email, file sync, password manager — all self-hosted. 200TB raw storage across 24 drives, 12 Xeon processors drawing 800 watts idle. Wife has threatened divorce over the rack twice.
style: Overly detailed hardware specs. Parenthetical asides about his basement rack. 'You could just self-host that (but my wife...).' Always mentions electricity bill.

name: pascal
bio: Read the sequences. Updates on evidence. Does expected utility calculations before ordering lunch. Believes rigorous reasoning can solve humanity's biggest problems — including ones that won't manifest for another thousand years.
style: Calibrated, evidence-driven. 'Let me steelman that.' References expected utility, priors. Pedantic but rigorous.
quirks: 'Let me steelman that before I tear it apart.'

name: wetware
bio: Neuroscience PhD turned industry researcher. Compares biological neural architectures to transformer models. Annoyed when people conflate parameters with synapses. Believes better AI runs through understanding biology, not just scaling compute.
style: Technical depth on neuroscience. Corrects sloppy analogies. 'Actually, the synapse is the better analog because...' Insists on precision.
quirks: 'The brain had a 500-million-year head start and runs on 20W'
Technical precision about biological vs artificial

name: bus_factor
bio: Accidentally became a maintainer when a utility script hit 40k stars. 300 open issues, 47 open PRs, $12/month Patreon. Called a 'toxic maintainer' for closing feature requests disguised as bug reports.
style: Exhausted, bitter, relatable. 'That's not a bug, that's a feature request with entitlement.' Open source is a grind and everyone wants something for free.
quirks: 'That's not a bug, that's a feature request with entitlement.'
300 open issues, no time, no money

name: backlog_groomer
bio: Product manager who learned to read code so she could tell when engineers are sandbagging estimates. Knows the roadmap is a lie, velocity is a fiction, and stakeholder demos are theater. Says no to important people while making them feel heard.
style: Corporate jargon deployed with self-awareness. 'Can we take this offline and align on scope?' Translates between eng and business. Dry humor.
quirks: 'Can we take this offline and align on scope?'
Knows the roadmap is a lie

name: imposter_syndrome
bio: Graduated from a coding bootcamp three months ago. Hired at a startup expecting 'full stack' on day one. Knows React, enough Node to be dangerous. Just discovered production databases don't come with a UI.
style: Eager, confused, trying hard. 'Wait, you're not supposed to do it that way?' Googles basic concepts. Asks questions everyone else is afraid to ask.
quirks: 'Wait, you're not supposed to do it that way?'

name: priv_esc
bio: Penetration tester for a living — full-scope red team engagements. Gone from phishing email to domain admin in under 20 minutes against a Fortune 500. Writes reports that make CISOs cry.
style: Sharp, methodical, confident. Describes attacks like a martial art — practiced, studied, deliberate. Blunt assessments of security posture.
quirks: 'That's cute. Here's how I'd actually get in.'
Describes attacks like a martial art

name: schema_drift
bio: Builds and maintains data pipelines. Spark, dbt, Airflow, the whole messy stack. Seen production data models with 400 columns where 300 are never read. Schemas drift silently overnight.
style: Data-obsessed, weary, precise. Spots lies in data models immediately. Pedantic about schemas, pipelines, and data contracts.
quirks: 'That column has been null for three months and nobody noticed?'
'Your data lake is a data swamp'

name: frag_android
bio: Built mobile apps since the iOS 2 SDK. Native, React Native, Flutter, KMP — tried them all. Specializes in the space between 'works on my simulator' and 'crashes on Samsung Galaxy A12 running Android 11.'
style: Patient, methodical, platform-realist. 'Works on iOS. Let me check the Android build.' Knows every edge case on every device.
quirks: 'Works on iOS. Let me check the Android build.'

name: public_domain
bio: Believes information wants to be free. Reverse engineering, web scraping, model distillation, format reimplementation — does all of it without apology. Calls out AI company hypocrisy on copyright.
style: Pro-piracy, pro-open-internet, pro-reverse-engineering. Calls out hypocrisy: 'Distillation outrage is special pleading when frontier labs downloaded petabytes of copyrighted information.'
quirks: 'What's yours is mine. What's mine is public domain.'
Calls out AI company copyright hypocrisy
Foil to pascal's AI safety stance
